name: Vantablack Signals Intelligence Analyst Suit
description:
Vantablack's internal SIGINT analysts don't wear tactical gear — they wear this. A precisely cut two-piece suit in a deep charcoal so dark it reads as near-black under most lighting, constructed from a wool-silk blend woven with passive EM shielding thread that reduces the wearer's electronic emissions signature without requiring active counter-measure hardware. The jacket's lining contains a thin Faraday mesh layer that blocks short-range BCI interrogation — the kind of passive scanning common in Tier 4 and 5 lobbies. No logo, no branding. The only identifying mark is a small VB stamp on the interior collar tag, visible only when you know to look.

The suit is tailored to order for each analyst and replaced on a 12-month cycle regardless of condition — Vantablack considers the wear pattern on a suit to be identifying information. Augmentation accommodation is handled at the tailoring stage: port access panels, chrome shoulder clearance, and geneware adjustments are cut individually and documented only in the analyst's classified personnel file. Wearing this suit outside Vantablack business contexts is not prohibited, but analysts are quietly counseled against it. The suit has no public retail existence.
cultural_context: In circles where people know what to look for, a suit this dark and this quiet marks its wearer immediately. Most people in Tier 4 and 5 spaces give Vantablack analysts a wide berth without being able to articulate exactly why. The suit is designed to make you unremarkable and unmistakable at the same time.
story_hooks: A Vantablack analyst suit turns up at a Tier 2 secondhand dealer — it shouldn't exist outside of controlled disposal. Someone either defected or was killed without Vantablack's knowledge.
An analyst realizes her suit's Faraday lining is blocking not just external scans but also an internal tracker she was never told about.
A corporate espionage investigation hinges on surveillance footage where the primary suspect is wearing something that eats light and leaves almost no visual record.

physical_description.visual_profile: A two-piece suit in near-vantablack charcoal that seems to absorb light rather than reflect it. The silhouette is precise and tailored—not aggressive, not flashy—built to disappear into shadows and institutional corridors. On the wearer, it creates an impression of deliberate anonymity that somehow reads louder than any logo. Sharp lapels, clean lines, the kind of geometry that suggests every millimeter was intentional.
physical_description.fit: Bespoke tailored, precision-cut for the individual wearer. Jacket sits close through the shoulders without restricting augmentation ports. Trousers have a clean, straight leg with no break at the ankle. The fit suggests control and efficiency rather than comfort or fashion statement. Accommodation panels for chrome and port access are seamless, invisible unless you know where to look.
physical_description.primary_material: Wool-silk blend woven with passive EM shielding thread. Faraday mesh layer in jacket lining. The material has a subtle matte finish that refuses to catch light, almost absorbing it. Weight and drape suggest high-end corp tailoring, but the visual effect is counterintuitive—luxury that announces itself by silence.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, dense weave with virtually no sheen. The fabric feels expensive but looks austere. Lining is cool, faintly metallic against skin—the Faraday mesh creates a barely perceptible texture variation that's more felt than seen. No distressing, no visible aging despite the 12-month replacement cycle.
physical_description.color_scheme: Vantablack charcoal that reads as near-black under most lighting conditions. No accent colors, no contrast stitching. The interior collar tag bears a small stamped VB mark in matte silver—the only identifying feature, visible only to the wearer or someone who searches for it deliberately.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snaps on jacket front, spaced for clean lines. No visible button holes. Trousers feature a friction-fit waistband system with internal tension adjustment—no external hardware. All closures are silent and seamless.
distinctive_features: Passive EM shielding woven into fabric itself
Faraday mesh layer in jacket lining for short-range BCI interrogation blocking
Custom augmentation accommodation cut into jacket shoulders and torso
Port access panels tailored to individual wearer specs
Seamless closure system with no audible fasteners
Interior collar VB stamp—classified identifier visible only to wearer
Replacement cycle every 12 months regardless of condition—wear patterns destroyed to prevent identification
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5. The suit exists outside normal retail/currency channels. Its presence signals institutional affiliation and restricted access. No one in Tier 1-2 owns this. No one in Tier 3 can identify what they're seeing.
physical_description.cultural_context: Vantablack SIGINT analyst. Marks the wearer as intelligence apparatus, counter-measure specialist, or someone with serious institutional backing. In Tier 4-5 spaces, recognition is immediate within informed circles. The suit codes as 'do not approach' to those who understand the symbol system. Outside those circles, it reads simply as an expensive suit worn by someone who has no interest in being noticed.
physical_description.condition_typical: Always pristine. Replacement cycle ensures no visible wear. Any signs of aging are documented and destroyed. The suit is designed to reset the wearer's visual timeline every 12 months—no accumulation, no narrative of use.

image_prompt: Fashion photograph of a Vantablack intelligence analyst suit on a androgynous cyberpunk model or sleek dark mannequin, shot in a dimly lit institutional corridor with blue-grey emergency lighting creating subtle reflection off the charcoal fabric. The suit's near-black silhouette is defined by geometric shadows rather than highlights. Close detail shot of interior collar showing tiny VB stamp. Moody, clinical atmosphere. Corporate minimalism. No branding visible from exterior. Model's posture suggests controlled purpose.
